metadata.title: Uber initiated, Thermo Fisher upgraded: Wall Street's top analyst calls

content.text:
The most talked about and market moving research calls around Wall Street are now in one place. Here are today's research calls that investors need to know, as compiled by The Fly.
Top 5 Upgrades:
-
UBS upgraded Thermo Fisher (TMO) to Buy from Neutral with a price target of $730, up from $540, after a transfer in analyst coverage. Thermo Fisher is positioned for a durable return to 5%-6%-plus organic growth in 2027, supported by improving pharma/biotech funding, bioprocessing demand, reshoring, AI-driven R&D investment, share gains, and stabilization in China and A&G, the firm tells investors in a research note.
-
BofA upgraded Figure Technology (FIGR) to Neutral from Underperform with a price target of $49, up from $31. The firm cites the company's stronger revenue growth outlook into 2028 due to Figure Connect momentum for the upgrade.
-
Wells Fargo upgraded Martin Marietta (MLM) to Overweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $609, up from $581. The firm cites the company's benefits to 2027 earnings from its recently closed Lhoist North America acquisition, plus pricing catch-up from the Quikrete asset swap and New Frontier acquisition for the upgrade.
-
Morgan Stanley upgraded Lineage (LINE) to Overweight from Equal Weight with an unchanged price target of $47. The firm believes the July 27 share lock-up expiration overhang and Tyson's revenue outlook cut create a "compelling" risk/reward for Lineage shares.
-
Jefferies upgraded Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) to Buy from Hold with a price target of $25, up from $15, ahead of HARMONi-3 progression-free survival data due late this year.
Top 5 Downgrades:
-
JPMorgan downgraded Dyne Therapeutics (DYN) to Underweight from Neutral with a price target of $10, down from $17. The firm believes Novartis' (NVS) Phase 3 trial miss for del-desiran in myotonic dystrophy type 1 puts Dyne's Phase 1/2 registrational expansion cohort evaluating z-basivarsen in DM1, which is expected to readout in Q1 of 2027, at risk.
-
Wells Fargo downgraded Vulcan Materials (VMC), Eagle Materials (EXP) and Amrize (AMRZ) to Underweight from Equal Weight with a price target of $254, down from $305. The firm also downgraded three names in construction materials citing an "increasingly cautious" 2027 outlook due to leaner government spending and higher interest rates.
-
BofA downgraded Patria Investments (PAX) to Underperform from Neutral with a price target of $10, down from $14, citing revised organic growth and expense assumptions. Patria is the largest private markets business in Latin America while Brazil remains its largest geography, notes the analyst, who says the firm's downgrade is "mostly driven" by geographic and macro factors.
-
BMO Capital downgraded Westlake (WLK) to Market Perform from Outperform with a price target of $82, down from $96. The firm cites leveled off commodity prices and mortgage rates reaching new highs for the downgrade.
-
Deutsche Bank downgraded Novartis (NVS) to Hold from Buy with a price target of CHF 120, down from CHF 140. The firm cites pelacarsen and del-desiran's miss for the downgrade.
